title: Identify where comfort problems occur
description: Note which rooms feel too hot or cold and check for noticeable gaps around doors and windows. Record the issue before deciding on property changes.
concerns: Drafts or rooms that feel too hot or cold
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now

title: Record your heating or cooling concern
description: Note which rooms are affected, when the problem happens, and which controls you can access. Use this information when discussing the issue with the equipment owner or a qualified professional.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now

title: Review lighting and electronics habits
description: Start with the lights and electronics you use most. Identify what is left on unnecessarily and which equipment you are permitted to change.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now

title: Review water-use habits
description: Review shower length, laundry settings, and whether you run full dishwasher or washing-machine loads. Separate changes to your habits from changes to installed equipment.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now

title: Identify the appliances behind your concern
description: List the appliances you use most and their available energy-saving settings. Note which appliances belong to you and which belong to the property owner.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now

title: Compare options before replacing equipment
description: Start with the equipment you already have: record its type, model, and the problem you want to solve, if that information is accessible. Check the manufacturer's energy-saving settings and instructions. If replacement is worth exploring, compare energy use, installation needs, and total cost—not just the purchase price. For heating or water-heating systems, ask a qualified professional whether the option suits your home.

title: Clarify equipment authority and prepare your concern summary
description: Record the equipment involved, the problem you want to solve, and when it occurs. If changes require approval, use this summary to start a discussion with the property owner or manager. If you are unsure who can authorize changes, clarify that before planning equipment work.
allowed_equipment_control: Only with landlord or property-manager approval

title: Plan an assessment before choosing comfort upgrades
description: List the rooms with drafts or uneven temperatures and when you notice the problem. Use a home energy assessment to explore whether air sealing, insulation, or another improvement is appropriate. If you rent, ask your landlord or property manager about arranging an assessment before planning property changes.
concerns: Drafts or rooms that feel too hot or cold

title: Make a lighting and electronics upgrade shortlist
description: Start with lights and electronics you use most. Record existing bulb types and device models where accessible. For future bulb purchases, compare brightness in lumens and check fixture compatibility. Review device power-saving settings before buying replacements. Separate items you own from fixtures or equipment that need the property owner's approval.

title: Get ready to explore energy programs
description: Have your location, utility provider, and rent/own status ready. Describe the issue you want to address. Before buying equipment or scheduling work, check the program's requirements and who needs to apply or approve changes.
concerns: Drafts or rooms that feel too hot or cold
